free_tier.stated: 6 GB free. Premium includes 10 TB base storage (expandable for purchase). No free route to >=500 GB: the free tier is 6 GB flat.

egress.terms: Metered twice over. Free accounts have a daily downstream quota; every account, free or paid, has a monthly Basic Transfer Quota, and 'Connected Apps share 25% of this daily allowance — up to 5 GB per day for all Connected Apps combined'. Downstream counts playback and previews, not just downloads.

tooling: Tier 1 rclone backend since v1.62, read-only for uploads? No — backend supports read and write per rclone's table (ModTime R, hash md5). This is the crucial detail: rclone is classified as a 'Connected App', so it inherits the 5 GB/day cap.
chaining: 10 TB per paid account is the largest single-unit paid capacity found in this slot, and it is the only one where the transfer cap (5 GB/day via Connected Apps / 20 GB/day general downstream) is stricter than the storage cap. Sharding accounts multiplies storage but not the per-account daily egress.

limits.value: reviews and online playback burn downstream quota, so scrape-style read patterns drain

limits_note: per-ip-shaping / pull-count hybrid: 20 GB/day downstream on free, 5 GB/day for all Connected Apps combined, monthly transfer quota on top. Free tier 6 GB storage. This provider is the cleanest illustration that quota and egress must be scored separately.
reliability_note: Transfer accounting is aggressive: previews and online playback burn downstream quota, so scrape-style read patterns drain it without any download. Price differs by region (US $4.99/mo Premium, Japan JPY 700, 'Global Premium' $9.99/mo).
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
